editorial:
Imagine being a star athlete in high school and then losing almost everything in a split second. That is exactly what happens to Chris, who suffers a bad brain injury in a car crash. Now, he struggles with his memory and has to write everything down just to get through the day. He finds a quiet job as a night janitor at a bank, trying his best to fit back into a world that feels strange to him. The vibe is quiet and a bit sad at first, but it quickly turns into a tense game of cat and mouse when some criminals realize Chris is the perfect person to help them rob the place because he is so easy to manipulate.

What really makes this work is the acting; you truly feel for Chris as he tries to figure out who to trust. The plot keeps you guessing, though it moves a bit slow in the middle before hitting a wild finish. If you like smart crime stories that focus on the people rather than just the action, you will love this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the bank scenes.
endingExplained: The big twist is that Chris is not as confused as everyone thinks. He actually remembers much more than he lets on. He tricks the robbers by pretending to help them, but he is actually working with the police the whole time. In the end, the criminals get caught in a trap he helped set. Chris finally gets some peace and proves he is much smarter than the people who tried to use him.
toneAndPace: slow start, tense middle, fast ending
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heist movies with a twist.
